label: token right after an early-middle p (original phase, t=3-6)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the step right after a p was input, but only when that p sits at original positions 2-5 (so t = 3-6). It is almost never active at t<3 or t>=8 and never in the copy phase. Precision is about 0.94 and the rule covers about 83% of activation mass. Strength depends on position: it is strongest at t=4-5 (p at position 3-4; the top examples are all p at position 3), weaker at t=3, and at t=6 it is weak and fires only some of the time. The identity of the current input token does not matter. Predicate misses: (1) a weaker follow-on activation two steps after the p, which adds about 9% of mass when included but lowers precision; (2) many tiny diffuse activations at t=4-5 with no p nearby. It does not fire on the <DEL> step after a p (those are mostly false positives) or on copy-phase steps.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: p, 1, j, b, 3, f; least: x, w, c, e) and the input two steps back (most: p, q, n, 2, a, f; least: x, c, e, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=5, t=6.
